title: Tiruvadi inscription of Ravivarman ; A.D. 1313
html:
TIRUVADI INSCRIPTION OF RAVIVARMAN ;
A.D. 1313.

BY PROFESSOR E. HULTZSCH, PH.D.; HALLE (SAALE).

This inscription (No. 34 of 1903) is engraved on the south wall of the Viraṭṭāṇesvara shrine at Tiruvadi near Panṇruṭṭi in the Cuddalore tāluka of the South Arcot district. It consists of a passage in the Sanskrit language and the Grantha alphabet, and of a sentence in the Tamil language and alphabet.

The Sanskrit portion (ll. 1-3) is identical with the first four lines of the Raṅganātha inscription of Ravivarman, which has been published and translated by Professor Kielhorn,1 as far as the word Kulasēkharadēva. The Tamil portion (l. 3 f.) records that Ravivarman alias Kulasēkharadēva bathed and repaired the central shrine of the Tiruviraṭṭāṇam temple at Tiruvadigai2 in the fourth year of his reign, the Kaliyuga year 4414 and the Śa[ka] year 12]35, on the day of Rôhiṇi, Saturday, the eleventh tithi of the first fortnight of Makara.

Professor Kielhorn kindly informs me that this date corresponds to Saturday, the 29th December A.D. 1313, when the 11th tithi of the bright half ended 6 h. 14 m., and the nakshatra was Rôhiṇi for about 21 hours, after mean sunrise.

In verse 4 of the Arulāla-Perumâl inscription of the same king we are told that he stayed at Kâñchî in his fourth year.3 The subjoined inscription is dated in the same year, and adds the information that this year corresponded to A.D. 1313.

TEXT.4

1 Svasti śrī-Jayasi[m]ha ity=abhihitas=Sômânvay-ôttainsakô râj=âśid=iha Kêralêshu vishayê nâthô Yadu-kshmâbhritâm || jâtô=smâd=Raviva[r]mma-bhûpatir=Um[â]dêvyâm kumâras=śivâd=dêhavyâpya-Śakâbda-bhâji samayê dêh=iva vîrô ra[sa]h ø [1*] Kshayan=nîtvâ sô=yam kali-bala[m=iv=âr]âti-nivaha[ñ]=ja[ya*]śrîvat kritvâ nija-sahacharîm Pâṇdya-tanayâm || trayastrimśad-va[r]shô yaśa i[va] yayau Kêrala-padam(dain) raraksha svam râshtra[n=na]garam=iva Kôlambam=adh[i]pah ø [2*] [Ji]tvâ Samgrâmadhirô nripatir=adhira[ṇa]m(ṇaṇ) vidvisham(sham) Vira-Pâṇdyam(ṇdyam) kritv=âsau Pâṇdya-Chôlân=naya iva tanum[â]n Kêralêbhyô=py=adhî[n]ân || shatcha-

2 tvârimśad-abdas=taṭa-bhuvi mukuṭan=dhârayan=Vêgavatyâh krîđâm simhâsana-sthas=chiram=akrita mahî-kîrtti-vâṇî-ramâbhih ø [3*] Â Mêrôr=â Malayâd=â pûrvvâd=â cha paśchimâd=acha[l]ât || Yadukula-sêkhara êsha kshôṇîm Kulasêkharas=svayam bubhujê || ø [4*] ø Svasti śrī [||*] Chandrak[ula-maṅgala]pradîpa || Yâdava-Nârâyaṇa || Kêraladêsa-puṇyapariṇâma || Nâmântara-Karṇṇa || Kûpaka-[s]ârvvabhauma || Kulasîkhari-pratishthâpita-Garuđaddhvaja || Kôlamba-puravar-âdhîsvara [||] Śrī-Patma(dma)nâbha-padakamala-paramârâdhaka [||] Prapatarâja-pratishthâchâryya || Vimatarâja-bandîkâra || Dharmmataru-mûlaka[nda] || Satgu(dgu)ṇ-âlamîkâra || [Cha]tushshashti-

3 kalâ-va[lla]bha || Dakshiña-Bhôjarâja | Sa[m]grâmadhira || Mahârâjâdhirâja-paramêsvara || Jayasimhadêva-nandana || Ravivarmma-mahârâja || [ol] Šrí [||] ol Šrí-Kulasêkharadêva || ol [I]varċku yâṇdu nâlâvadu Kaliyuga-varsham 4414 idil nîngiya Ša . . . ! . 355 idaṇ mêl šellâniṇra Magara-nâyarĵu pûrvva-pakshattu êkâdaśiyum Šaṇi-kki[la]m[aiyum] p[e]rra Rôsaṇ[i]-nâ! Tiruvadi[g]ai uđaiyâr Tiru[vira]tjtâṇam-uđaiya nâyaṇâr kôyil Vâṇa-Kaiyilâya-Ttirumalai stûpi-paryyantamâga tirumañjaṇamum paṇpi [pu]rachchârapai tirukkallum ś[ât]ti-

4 y-aru[i]ṇâr Raviva[r]mma-ma[h]ârâ[ja]r-âṇa perumâ! Kulasêgaradêvar ol Svasti śrí ol

TRANSLATION OF THE TAMIL PORTION.

(Line 3.) (In) the fourth year of this (king),— the Kaliyuga year 4414,— the Ša[ka] year 12]35 separated from this,6— on the day of Rôhiṇi, which corresponded to a Saturday and to the eleventh tithi of the first fortnight of the month Makara current after this (Šaku year),— Ravivarma-Mahârâja alias the lord Kulasêkharadêva was pleased to bathe up to the pinnacle the Vâṇa-Kaiyilâya-Tirumalai7 (in) the temple of the lord of Tiruvirattâṇam, the god of Tiruvadigai, and to fix the stones which were bulging out. Hail! Prosperity!

Footnotes

1↩(p. 8, n. 1) Above, Vol. IV. p. 149.

2↩(p. 8, n. 2) For this ancient name of Tiruvadi see above, Vol. VII. p. 162.

3↩(p. 8, n. 3) Above, Vol. IV. p. 147.

4↩(p. 8, n. 4) From an inked estampage prepared by Mr. G. Venkoba Rao.

5↩(p. 9, n. 1) Restore Šakdâdam 1235.

6↩(p. 9, n. 2) The meaning of this expression is perhaps: 'separately stated along with this (Kaliyuga year).'

7↩(p. 9, n. 3) I.e. 'the holy mountain of the heavenly Kailâsa.' This seems to have been the name of the central shrine in the Tiruvirattâṇam temple.
